dedupe_keys.name: faa aviation environmental design tool aedt

description: The Aviation Environmental Design Tool (AEDT) is the FAA's software system for modelling aircraft performance in space and time to estimate fuel consumption, emissions, noise and air quality consequences. It is required for FAA environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act and scales from a single airport to regional, national and global studies, using a GIS and a relational database. It is developed for the FAA Office of Environment and Energy. The support site states that AEDT 4b was released on 16 September 2026 (build 258.0.26722.1) and is required for FAA actions from that date; it adds noise modelling with structures for research use, AERMOD, AERMET and AERSURFACE version 26135, and BADA 3.8 and BADA 4.3 aircraft performance. Coverage: any airport or airspace, with an aircraft fleet database. Format and access: licensed desktop software. Licence and cost: paid seats; the site gives an upgrade price of 170 US dollars per seat from AEDT 3, while AEDT 4a users upgrade to 4b free. Caveats: the tool is licensed, Windows-based and tied to FAA regulatory methods. It supports capacity planning of airports and airspace with noise and emissions limits, and climate studies of aviation. It relates to the EUROCONTROL BADA performance model, the ICAO engine emissions databank and the BTS national transportation noise map in the catalogue.
